requirement: The same Idempotency-Key with the same fingerprint returns the one existing operation and hires nobody twice; the same key with a changed body is 409 idempotency_conflict.
why_it_matters: backend-v1.4.md §5.2. A retried spawn is the most expensive duplicate in the product: it starts a second agent, in a second pane, holding the same task. Uniqueness is (auth-session scope, key) — deliberately not including kind or target, so reusing one key for a different action is detected rather than slipping past.

documents.name: the request body, sent twice with Idempotency-Key spawn-checkout-1

assert.note: the agent does not exist yet; the target names only what the caller already knew

documents.name: replay — same key, same fingerprint: the SAME operation, not a second hire

assert.note: same identity as the first call — this is the whole point

value.detail: Idempotency-Key spawn-checkout-1 was used for agent.spawn with a different body (role reviewer, was coder). Nothing was spawned.

counterexamples.name: the replay started a second agent
counterexamples.why: A fresh operation_id for the same key and body means the reservation was not honoured: two agents now hold the same task in two panes. The shape is valid, so only the idempotency rule catches it.

counterexamples.name: an operation whose target leaks the resolved pane
counterexamples.why: OperationTarget carries only local ids the caller already named. A pane id is a server-resolved tmux target; echoing it back would hand the browser an argument it must never be able to supply (SHARED wire decision 8).
